articles.title: The Best Wireless Earbuds of 2026, Tested and Reviewed
articles.summary: I tested more than 50 wireless earbuds to select our top picks. Shop brands like Apple, Beats, Bose and more.
articles.body: I’m always testing earbuds and have tried more than 50 options for this story. I use wireless earbuds constantly to tune out noise on the subway, to listen to a podcast, take calls at work, listen to music while I work out — I always have a pair in my backpack or my pocket. With so many options, it can be hard to know which model is best for you and your needs. Below, I rounded up the best wireless earbuds for various activities and budgets so you can find a pair that most suits your lifestyle. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best wireless earbuds After testing dozens of earbuds, my top picks came from brands like Apple, Google, Beats, Bose and Shokz. Every option on this list were samples I requested from brands for testing purposes for this story. You can find key specifications like battery life and IP rating inside the "What to know" dropdown. In May, I updated this list after testing the Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro. Best for iPhone If you own an iPhone, these are the earbuds to get. They are comfortable, have excellent sound quality and noise cancellation features. They’re also good for basically any activity you throw at them including outdoor runs and workouts. With noise cancellation turned on, chatter and music at the gym fade instantly, in my experience. With transparency mode on, I can hear my surroundings very clearly, perfect for running outdoors. The buds have great on-ear controls, including a swipe on the ear stem to control volume. They also have built-in heart rate sensors, meaning you can start a workout from your iPhone and track your heart rate and calories burned with just your AirPods Pro 3 — no fitness tracker required. They come with five ear tip sizes, more than most brands, which can help you get a more comfortable fit for your ears. If all of this sounds good to you, but you can’t stand rubber eartips clogging your ears, consider Apple AirPods 4 ANC instead. They have similarly great sound and call quality, but leave your ears more open because they don’t have rubber eartips. However, the noise cancellation is less effective than AirPods Pro 3, in my experience. Best for Android Anyone with an Android phone looking for one pair of do-it-all earbuds should consider these latest Google Pixel buds. The new design has a mini wing-tip stabilizer in each ear that fits snugly and makes them stable and secure for workouts. “They are comfortable and don’t hurt the inside of my ear within an hour of wearing them,” says NBC Select commerce editor Cory Fernandez. Best budget You don’t need to spend hundreds of dollars to get fully featured earbuds — these have active noise cancelling, transparency mode, Bluetooth multipoint and wireless charging, all for under $100. They are comfortable, sound surprisingly good and can compete with earbuds that are much pricier. The only downside is noise cancellation — it’s okay, but isn’t very useful against plane, train and car noise. The Liberty 4 NC is not the brand’s latest model, and while I would love to recommend the newer Anker Soundcore Liberty 5, which are excellent, they are $130, which I don’t consider “budget.” Best affordable earbuds These are some of the most affordable wireless earbuds that still deliver a steady Bluetooth connection, surprisingly good sound quality and a convenient charging case. The earbuds and case have a combined battery life of around 32 hours, and the case has a cable built-in for convenient recharging. If you purchase the earbuds from the brand’s website, you can choose from 13 bright and earth-tone colorways. They don’t have active noise cancelling or transparency modes, and the app is a little lackluster, but these are fair trade-offs for such a low price. Best noise cancellation If your top priority is blocking out background noise like the hum of a plane cabin, rattling train cars and water cooler talk, these earbuds are for you. They have the best noise cancellation of any earbud I’ve tried, full stop. Plus they sound amazing, with detailed instrumentation in music and clear audio in TV shows and movies. They are big earbuds, though — I don’t find them particularly comfortable for fitness and exercise. They are also pricey at $300. If you’re willing to sacrifice a little noise cancelling power, consider the Bose QuietComfort Earbuds as a more affordable runner-up. Best for fitness The previous Beats Fit Pro were my go-to workout headphones for years, and the updated version, these Beats Powerbeats Fit, make a few subtle improvements but keep everything I loved about the originals in-tacts. The buds have a wing-tip design that creates a secure fit in your ear — mine stay secure during runs, bike rides and gym time. They are small and relatively lightweight compared to other earbuds on this list, but are especially compact compared to sportier, full ear-hook earbuds like the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2. Both earbuds have physical button controls that are easy to use, even when I am wearing thick gloves during a winter run. You can press either button to stop, start and skip songs, and holding the button changes between noise cancellation and transparency mode. They pair easily with iPhones and Android phones (through the Beats app). Best open ear Open earbuds rest on the outside of your ear instead of going inside of your ear canal. I use them on bike rides while NBC Select editorial director Lauren Swanson uses them for runs and races like the New York City Marathon — it makes it easier to hear nearby cars, bikes and pedestrians. While I’m partial to the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, I admit that the more versatile option for everyday use is the Shokz OpenFit 2. They are small and comfortable, have great sound quality (for open earbuds) and fit in a relatively pocketable charging case. But, like with any pair of open earbuds, don’t expect them to block any noisy neighbors while working out at the gym. The Shokz OpenFit 2 don’t have wireless charging. If that’s a crucial feature for you, get the Shokz OpenFit 2+ instead. Best clip on A newer offshoot of open earbuds is clip-on earbuds. These earbuds wrap around your outer ear like an ear cuff, leaving your ear canal open and the top of your ears free for things like glasses and hats. The Bose Ultra Open Earbuds are some of the best clip-on earbuds I’ve tried (with a price tag to match). They don’t look very secure at a glance, but after multiple 5Ks and 15 plus mile bike rides, they are some of the most secure open earbuds you can get. They are also comfortable, lightweight and unobtrusive — I wore them for a full day and forgot they were on my ears multiple times. Clip-on earbuds don’t have the best sound quality — the speakers are further away from your ears. While audio quality on the Ultra Open Earbuds is good, call quality isn’t great. You can learn more in my Bose Ultra Open Earbuds review. If you aren’t completely sold on clip-on earbuds, consider trying the Anker Soundcore C40i, JLab Flex Open or Soundpeats Pop Clip earbuds instead — they are all much cheaper, but have a similar shape and size to the Ultra Open. Best earhook The Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 are some of the most secure workout headphones I’ve ever tested. The earhook design and general fit take a minute to set into your ear, but once they’re settled, they are rock solid and don’t budge no matter what I am doing. The earbuds have noise cancellation and transparency modes, on ear media and volume controls, a wireless charging case and work well on both iPhone and Android devices. They also have built-in heart rate sensors in each earbud, and while a little finicky to sync, they are nice to have if you don’t already use a fitness tracker or smart ring. You can read more in my Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 review. My previous earhook pick, the JBL Endurance Peak 3, is still a great option if you are looking for something simple, secure and less pricey. Best cheap earhook For $30, I was surprised by the quality of these earbuds. They have a large ear hook design that wraps around the back of your ears — I found them to be tight and comfortable, but not so snug that I couldn’t hear traffic noise or other runners around me. Plus they have a transparency mode and customizable settings through the JLab app. I think these are best as a second pair of earbuds you use specifically for working out or going for a run. You can be a little more carefree with a $30 pair of earbuds than a $300 pair. Other notable earbuds I tested Sony WF-1000XM6: These Sony earbuds are some of the best sounding options on the market, with impressive noise cancelling and transparency modes, plus a very customizable app. The $330 price tag is very steep, though, especially compared to the also-excellent Apple AirPods Pro 3 and Google Pixel Buds Pro 2. Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro: If you love your Samsung smartphone, these Samsung earbuds are also worth considering. They are comfortable and sound excellent, similar to the Apple AirPods Pro 3 and Google Pixel Buds Pro 2. They are also IP57 dust and water resistant — that’s a much higher rating than most of its competitors. Shokz OpenDots One: These clip-on earbuds are a worthwhile alternative to the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds. They are comfortable, reliable and cost less. I did prefer the on-ear controls and overall fit and finish of the Bose, however. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 are one of the best open ear headphones for outdoor fitness activity: full stop. I recommend the Shokz OpenFit 2 above because they are a bit more versatile and convenient with their smaller size and portable charging case. But if you are a runner or cyclist looking for headphones optimized for those activities, these are what you should get. Anker Soundcore Liberty 5: The Liberty 5 earbuds are newer than the Liberty 4 NC, with longer battery life (up to 12 hours) and better dust and water resistance (IP55). But they are $130, and on sale for less of a discount than the Liberty 4 NC typically are. How I test wireless earbuds I’m always testing new earbuds by incorporating them into my daily routine. That includes office work, video calls, subway commutes, outdoor runs, indoor gym time and watching videos on my phone, tablet or laptop. While using earbuds, I pay close attention to the following factors: Comfort: A pair of earbuds is only useful if you feel comfortable wearing them for hours at a time. I wore earbuds for upwards of 3 hours to get a feel for long-term comfort. I also tried different-sized ear tips to find my ideal fit. Everyone’s ears are a little different. If the earbuds don’t fit comfortably right out the box, try different eartips to get a more comfortable fit.Noise cancellation: I used each pair of earbuds for my office commute on the NYC subway. I also used them in-office to block out background noise and conversations.Sound quality: I listened to the same music playlist with each pair of earbuds to identify differences in sound quality and instrumentation.Ease of use: When trying earbuds, I used the on-ear controls to take calls, play media and more. I also downloaded each brand’s mobile app, noting how easy it was to use and the utility offered. Some earbuds let you connect to multiple devices at the same time, this is called Bluetooth multipoint — I tried this feature with my phone, tablet and laptop when available.Battery life: I tried each pair of earbuds for at least a week. Throughout that period, I paid attention to how many times I needed to charge them. How to shop for wireless earbuds There are hundreds of wireless earbuds on the market. Some can look almost identical, but they can vary wildly in features and price. Below are a few factors to keep in mind while shopping for a new pair. Operating System (iPhone and Android) Not all wireless earbuds play nice with both Apple and Android devices. If you use Apple AirPods on an Android device, for example, most of their features will be difficult or impossible to use. Earbuds that work well on both platforms tend to have useful standalone apps that can help control noise cancellation, audio equalization and more. Automated noise cancelling and transparency Noise cancelling and transparency modes are both useful features that add versatility to any pair of earbuds. Noise cancelling blocks outside sound, while transparency mode lets sound in so you can better hear the noise around you, a useful safety feature for activities like outdoor running. Cheaper earbuds (under $100) may have one or both built-in, but generally don’t perform as well as pricier options. (under $250). Water and dust resistance Water and dust resistance is indicated by an earbud’s IP (ingress protection) rating. IP ratings are denoted with two numbers, for example, IP55. The first digit represents intrusion protection against dust and debris. The second digit denotes moisture protection. If you want to wear your earbuds in wet and rainy conditions, get a pair with a higher IP rating, they are less likely to malfunction in bad weather. Why trust NBC Selected? I am a reporter at NBC Selected who covers technology and fitness including stories on fitness trackers, over-ear headphones and point-and-shoot cameras. I’ve been testing earbuds and headphones for years — I try new models constantly, comparing them against previous versions and similar competitors. For a varied perspective, everybody has different ears, after all, I also spoke with other NBC Select staffers about their experience using wireless earbuds. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: UK petrol prices hit highest level since Iran war began
articles.summary: The price of unleaded hits 163p a litre, according to motoring group the RAC, as oil prices remain elevated.
articles.body:
UK petrol prices have risen to their highest level since the beginning of the Iran war as the conflict continues to hit drivers' finances.

The average cost of petrol has reached more than 163p per litre, according to motoring group the RAC, which warned prices could climb higher yet.

The price of fuel tends to track the wholesale price of oil, which surged when the Iran conflict began on 28 February. The fighting has severely disrupted oil supplies across the Middle East.

Prices then nosedived when US and Iran agreed to a framework deal to end the conflict in June, but they have risen again since the collapse of peace talks.

How do wholesale oil prices affect the cost of petrol and diesel at the pump?

Crude oil is a key ingredient in petrol and diesel, which means that higher wholesale costs make filling up a car more expensive. The price of petrol and diesel is also heavily influenced by demand and refining capacity.

Analysts say every $10 (£7.44) per barrel increase in the oil price pushes up pump prices by roughly 7p a litre.

Since the war began, the price of a barrel of Brent crude – the global benchmark for wholesale oil prices – has been very volatile.

Generally speaking, news of further conflict drives the price up while hopes of an end to the war pushes the price down.

Before the conflict, Brent was about $70 a barrel, but the fighting saw it peak at above $120.

In early July, after the framework deal was signed, prices fell back to near the $70 a barrel mark.

When the peace talks collapsed, the price climbed back up again to above $100 a barrel, but are now around $94.

What has happened to petrol and diesel prices in the UK?

While petrol has hit its highest price since the Iran war began, according to the RAC, diesel remains below the peak of 191.54p a litre it reached on 15 April.

In early July, the RAC said the average price of petrol sank to a low of 150.59p per litre and 164.52p per litre for diesel.

Since then the prices have risen, with petrol now at 163.6p a litre while diesel costs 184.99p a litre.

RAC's head of policy Simon Williams said that, with oil prices remaining elevated, drivers will "almost certainly start paying noticeably more at the pumps in the coming weeks".

Despite the conflict, petrol and diesel prices remain below the levels reached in the summer of 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, when petrol reached 191.5p a litre and diesel hit 199p.

Because transporting oil is a slow process, price movements in the wholesale markets take about a fortnight to show at the pump.

Fuel retailers have denied accusations of price gouging during the conflict. The official markets regulator said it had "not seen evidence of retailers actively changing their pricing strategies to take advantage of the crisis".

A government scheme called Fuel Finder lets drivers compare the cost of fuel offered by petrol stations across the UK.

Luke Bosdet, the head of policy at the AA, said the group had been surprised at the speed that prices had fallen and put it down to the scheme.

In May, the then Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer said a planned 5p increase in fuel duty due in September would be postponed until the end of December because of the conflict.

No evidence of widespread fuel price-gouging, watchdog says

Drivers can compare fuel prices at different petrol stations - how does it work?

Why has the Iran war had a big impact on oil prices?

The Middle East conflict sent global oil prices soaring as it effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's key water transport routes for oil, liquid natural gas and other essential commodities — limiting global supplies.

About 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas normally passes through the waterway.

Even if a deal is agreed to reopen the strait, experts warn it will take time before normal levels of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz resume, and the impact of the war will continue to affect the global economy for potentially months to come.

Why and how is US blockading Iranian ports in Strait of Hormuz?

Oil price predicted to remain above $100 for rest of year

The UK is heavily reliant on oil and gas imports, with the majority coming from the US and Norway.

The price of oil on the global market determines how much the UK pays for it.

Although the UK does get some oil from the North Sea, most of that is exported for refining elsewhere.

Reporting by Faarea Masud, Jemma Crew, Alex Daniel, Michael Race, Mitchell Labiak, and Miguel Roca-Terry

articles.title: Carlos Machado (PCB) propõe reduzir alunos por sala e moradias em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Representante do PCB também defendeu ampliação do número de leitos, concursos para professores e combate à lavagem de dinheiro de facções criminosas em entrevista à EPTV.
articles.summary: Carlos Machado (PCB) propõe ampliar leitos, realizar concursos e combater a lavagem de dinheiro de facções criminosas em seu plano para o governo de São Paulo.
articles.body:
Carlos Machado (PCB) , candidato ao governo de São Paulo, defendeu reduzir o número de estudantes por sala de aula e aumentar a oferta de moradias populares. As declarações foram exibidas nesta sexta-feira (4), em uma entrevista que integra a série da EPTV com os concorrentes ao Palácio dos Bandeirantes.

O formato de participação foi definido de acordo com o desempenho na pesquisa Quaest de 25 de agosto . Quem alcançou 5% ou mais das intenções de voto foi convidado para uma entrevista ao vivo, transmitida para as regiões de Campinas , Piracicaba , Ribeirão Preto e São Carlos.

Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) e Fernando Haddad (PT) atingiram esse percentual. A ordem de exibição foi definida por sorteio, na presença de representantes das campanhas.

Tarcísio seria o primeiro a participar, na segunda-feira (31), mas a assessoria informou na sexta-feira (28) que ele não compareceria. Haddad foi entrevistado ao vivo na terça-feira (1º).

Já os concorrentes que ficaram abaixo de 5% têm direito a entrevistas gravadas de dois minutos. Além de Machado, fazem parte desse grupo:

Policial Edjane abriu essa etapa na quarta-feira (2) . Vera Lúcia teve a entrevista exibida na quinta-feira (3) , e Carlos Machado participou nesta sexta-feira (4).

Carlos Machado tem 41 anos, é solteiro e nasceu em Franca (SP). É professor de ensino médio e tem ensino superior completo. Em 2024, foi candidato a vice-prefeito de Franca pelo PCB. Esta é a primeira vez que concorre ao governo de São Paulo.

Carlos Machado (PCB), candidato ao governo de São Paulo, em entrevista à EPTV — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Na segurança pública, Machado concentrou parte das propostas na violência contra a mulher e no enfrentamento às facções criminosas.

“Hoje a segurança pública é um grave problema, principalmente para as minorias. Nós tivemos um aumento muito grande do feminicídio e de violência contra a mulher, tivemos um corte de gastos gigantesco na delegacia das mulheres e nós precisamos revê-lo.”

Ao tratar do crime organizado, o candidato defendeu que a atuação do Estado também alcance a movimentação financeira das facções.

“Nós precisamos combater as facções criminosas de forma inteligente, lidando com a questão de crimes financeiros, principalmente lavagem de dinheiro.”

Machado disse ainda que o enfrentamento às facções deveria envolver a presença do poder público nos territórios.

“[É preciso] ampliar a capacidade do Estado de ocupar o território junto com a população com políticas públicas, como cultura, como educação, como esporte, como saúde.”

Na saúde, o candidato apresentou propostas voltadas à prevenção e à ampliação da capacidade de atendimento.

“A primeira medida que nós pensamos com relação à questão da saúde, primeiro, é articular os prefeitos para a gente poder ampliar a questão da saúde da família.”

Machado também citou a atuação nos bairros e a participação da população nas políticas da área.

“É fundamental uma saúde preventiva que atue nos bairros e também aí conectar isso à população a partir de conselhos populares de saúde.”

Sobre a estrutura de atendimento, o candidato afirmou que o número de leitos é insuficiente e defendeu a expansão da rede. Segundo Machado, são atualmente 1,8 leito por mil habitantes.

Na educação, Machado criticou o modelo adotado na rede de ensino e classificou a situação atual como de “desmonte” e “precarização”.

“A gente vê aí as plataformizações, a gamificação da educação e a primeira medida será acabar com isso.”

Entre as mudanças propostas pelo candidato está a expansão da rede. “E, a partir da ampliação da rede, diminuir o número de alunos por sala de aula.”

Machado também relacionou as propostas para a área às condições de trabalho e à remuneração dos profissionais.

“Fazer concurso público para funcionários e professores e poder ampliar o salário até no valor que é maior pago no Brasil, que é de R$ 13 mil.”

Na área de habitação, Machado associou a ampliação da oferta de moradias a medidas sobre o mercado imobiliário.

“Nós pretendemos fazer uma política firme de combate à especulação imobiliária e também ampliar as moradias populares via CDHU.”

articles.title: Enchente no Himalaia faz mais de 1,3 mil mortos e 5 mil desaparecidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Desastre provocado pelo colapso de uma geleira atingiu áreas da fronteira entre os dois países na semana passada
articles.summary: Desastre provocado pelo colapso de uma geleira atingiu áreas da fronteira entre os dois países na semana passada
articles.body:
As enchentes devastadoras na fronteira entre China e Nepal da última semana deixaram pelo menos 1.318 mortos e 5.624 desaparecidos , somando-se os dados das autoridades de gestão de desastres dos dois países nesta sexta-feira (4).

A imprensa estatal chinesa informou que 31 pessoas morreram no Tibete e que outras 531 estão desaparecidas. Já no Nepal, foram registradas 1.287 vítimas fatais e 5.083 paradeiros.

Equipes de resgate salvam dois trabalhadores presos em túnel

Equipes de resgate do Nepal encontraram com vida dois trabalhadores que estavam presos em um túnel de uma usina hidrelétrica nove dias após uma avalanche histórica que devastou o país, informaram autoridades nesta sexta-feira (4).

O primeiro sobrevivente foi retirado do túnel da usina hidrelétrica Trishul 3A durante uma operação conduzida pelo Exército nepalês. Pouco depois, um parlamentar do país afirmou que uma segunda pessoa também foi resgatada com vida.

Imagens compartilhadas pelo Exército mostraram um dos trabalhadores coberto de lama e sendo carregado nos ombros de um socorrista. Equipes médicas prestaram atendimento ainda no local do resgate e posteriormente os dois trabalhadores foram levados a um hospital em Katmandu.

“Não consigo explicar o que estamos sentindo neste momento. Estamos apenas gratos a Deus”, disse Amir Maharjan, irmão de um dos trabalhadores resgatados, à agência de notícias Associated Press (AP).

Autoridades acreditam que outras pessoas ainda possam estar vivas dentro do túnel. O ministro da Energia do Nepal, Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, afirmou à emissora britânica BBC esperar que mais pessoas sejam resgatadas no local nas próximas horas.

O desastre começou na última quarta-feira (26) , quando parte de uma geleira próxima ao pico Langtang Lirung, no Nepal, desabou. A queda arrastou grandes volumes de gelo e rochas e provocou uma avalanche que atingiu o rio Lhende Khola.

O material bloqueou o curso do rio e formou uma enorme onda de lama, pedras, gelo e água. O fluxo avançou por mais de 20 quilômetros e atingiu áreas do Nepal e do Tibete, destruindo vilarejos, estradas, pontes e instalações de energia.

Um dos locais mais atingidos foi o posto de fronteira de Gyirong, no Tibete. Imagens de câmeras de segurança registraram a força da enxurrada, que arrastou construções e pessoas. O local é uma importante ligação comercial entre a China e o Nepal.

Trabalhador resgatado após nove dias preso em túnel no Nepal. — Foto: Nepal Army via AP

articles.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa pelo governo do Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta sexta-feira (4) foi encomendada pela TV Verdes Mares e realizada entre os dias 31 de agosto e 3 de setembro. Margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta sexta-feira (4) foi encomendada pela TV Verdes Mares. Margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Ciro Gomes e Elmano de Freitas lideram a disputa pelo Governo do Ceará nas eleições 2026. — Foto: Sistema Verdes Mares

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta sexta-feira (4) mostra como está a disputa para o governo do Ceará. Na pesquisa estimulada, Ciro Gomes (PSDB) aparece com 45% das intenções de voto, enquanto o governador Elmano de Freitas (PT) aparece com 34%. O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Verdes Mares.

A pesquisa estimulada é aquela em que os nomes dos candidatos são apresentados aos eleitores. A diferença de Ciro para Elmano é de 9 pontos percentuais, portanto, acima da margem da erro - que é de 3 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos.

Números da pesquisa estimulada para 1º turno:

Veja, abaixo, os resultados da pesquisa estimulada para o 1º turno, em que a Quaest mostra a lista de candidatos aos eleitores entrevistados.

Para 67% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 31% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até as eleições, em 4 de outubro.

O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Verdes Mares e ouviu 900 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 31 de agosto e 3 de setembro. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95%. A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número CE-01149/2026.

A Quaest mostra também os resultados da pesquisa espontânea, em que os nomes dos candidatos não são mostrados aos eleitores, isto é, o candidato é citado de pelo próprio eleitor. Veja os números:

A Quaest também testou o cenário de 2º turno entre os candidatos Ciro Gomes e Elmano de Freitas. Confira:

22% dos eleitores dizem que o governador a ser eleito deve continuar o trabalho que vem sendo feito.

39% defendem mudar apenas o que não está bom.

35% consideram que é necessário mudar totalmente.

46% preferem que o governador eleito seja aliado de Lula

15% preferem um aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro

Se Lula apoiasse um candidato e pedisse seu voto, isso aumentaria sua chance de votar no candidato, diminuiria a chance de votar no candidato ou não mudaria nada? Veja os números:

37% dizem que o apoio de Lula aumenta a chance de votar no candidato

22% dizem que diminui a chance de votar no candidato

Se Flávio Bolsonaro apoiasse um candidato e pedisse seu voto, isso aumentaria sua chance de votar no candidato, diminuiria a chance de votar no candidato ou não mudaria nada? Veja os números:

14% dizem que o apoio de Flávio Bolsonaro aumenta a chance de votar no candidato

42% dizem que diminui a chance de votar no candidato

A Quaest perguntou aos eleitores qual é o principal problema do estado. Veja os temas mais citados:

A Quaest consultou também os eleitores sobre cada um dos candidatos: se eles conhecem e votariam, se não conhecem ou se conhecem e não votariam. Os candidatos mais rejeitados (maiores índices de "conhece e não votaria") são, respectivamente, Elmano de Freitas e Ciro Gomes.

articles.title: 500 kg de maconha na Via Dutra: homem é preso após perseguição | G1
articles.standfirst: Prisão foi realizada por agentes do Gabinete de Segurança Institucional do Governo do Estado (GSI-RJ) durante a "Operação Foco".
articles.summary: Durante a Operação Foco em Itatiaia, agentes do GSI-RJ apreenderam 500 kg de maconha após perseguição e confronto armado com criminosos na Via Dutra.
articles.body:
Homem é preso com mais de 500 kg de maconha após perseguição na Via Dutra, em Itatiaia — Foto: Governo do Estado do Rio de Janeiro

Um homem foi preso com cerca de 500 kg de maconha nesta sexta-feira (4), na Via Dutra, em Itatiaia (RJ). A prisão foi realizada por agentes do Gabinete de Segurança Institucional do Governo do Estado (GSI-RJ) durante a "Operação Foco".

Segundo o GSI-RJ, o caminhão passou pelo ponto de fiscalização e recebeu ordem de parada mas o condutor fugiu. Os agentes perseguiram o veículo e o encontraram perto do pedágio de Itatiaia.

Ainda de acordo com o Gabinete de Segurança Institucional do Governo do Estado, durante a abordagem, um veículo que acompanhava o caminhão se aproximou e os ocupantes atiraram contra os agentes.

O GSI-RJ informou ainda que os suspeitos que estavam no caminhão abandonaram o veículo e fugiram por uma área de mata, chegando a atravessar um rio que corta a região. Um dos homens foi encontrado e preso. O outro conseguiu fugir e está foragido.

O caminhão foi levado para o Posto Fiscal de Itatiaia, onde os agentes apreenderam a carga de maconha. O material ainda está sendo contabilizado, mas até o momento, foram pesados mais de 500 kg de maconha

O suspeito foi encaminhado para a delegacia de Itatiaia onde o caso foi registrado. O homem está à disposição da Justiça. A identidade do preso não foi divulgada.

Ônibus é atingido por tiro em Maricá — Foto: Redes Sociais

Um ônibus da Empresa Pública de Transportes (EPT) de Maricá , na Região Metropolitana do Rio, foi atingido por um tiro no parabrisa, na tarde desta quinta-feira (3).

Segundo a Prefeitura, o veículo estava estacionado em um ponto em Inoã durante a troca de turno e não havia passageiros nem motorista dentro do ônibus. Não houve feridos.

Ainda de acordo com a administração municipal, o ônibus fazia a linha E26, de Inoã a Itaipuaçu. O veículo foi retirado de circulação e substituído por outro.

articles.title: Motorista avança preferencial, mata motociclista e é presa em RO | G1
articles.standfirst: Condutora fugiu do local sem prestar socorro, mas foi localizada em casa pela polícia. Ela se recusou a fazer o teste do bafômetro, mas apresentava sinais visíveis de embriaguez.
articles.summary: Condutora fugiu do local sem prestar socorro, mas foi localizada em casa pela polícia. Ela se recusou a fazer o teste do bafômetro, mas apresentava sinais visíveis de embriaguez.
articles.body:
Uma mulher identificada como Stefanny Thalia Ferreira Liberato foi presa em flagrante após se envolver em um acidente de trânsito que resultou na morte de um motociclista, no bairro São João Bosco, zona Norte de Porto Velho , durante a madrugada desta sexta-feira (4). De acordo com o registro policial, ela confessou que bebeu, mas se recusou a fazer o teste do bafômetro.

Uma câmera de segurança registrou o momento da colisão. As imagens mostram quando a motorista avança a via preferencial em alta velocidade e atinge o motociclista (veja o vídeo acima). A motorista fugiu sem prestar socorro e foi localizada poucas quadras depois, na própria residência.

Os policiais relataram que ela apresentava sinais de alteração da capacidade psicomotora, como hálito com cheiro de álcool, olhos avermelhados, sonolência e dificuldade de equilíbrio. Os agentes também constataram que o veículo conduzido por ela estava com o licenciamento vencido.

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a motorista contou que saiu da faculdade e foi para um bar. Ela afirmou que antes de passar pelo cruzamento onde ocorreu o acidente engatou a quarta marcha e acelerou o veículo, momento em que aconteceu a colisão.

O motociclista foi socorrido pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e levado ao Hospital e Pronto-Socorro João Paulo II com sangramento intenso. A equipe médica informou à polícia que o homem não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu na unidade. A vítima não portava documentos e não havia sido identificada até o registro da ocorrência.

A Perícia Criminal realizou os procedimentos no local do acidente e Stefanny foi autuada por homicídio culposo na direção de veículo automotor com a agravante de embriaguez ao volante. A suspeita foi encaminhada à Central de Flagrantes e aguarda audiência de custódia.

articles.title: Avião com Mariana Fagundes fez pouso de emergência após gerador parar | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora seguia rumo ao Rio de Janeiro para gravar um programa de TV quando a aeronave apresentou problemas. Aeronave decolou no Pará e pouso em Goiânia na manhã de quinta-feira (3).
articles.summary: Cantora seguia rumo ao Rio de Janeiro para gravar um programa de TV quando a aeronave apresentou problemas.
articles.body:
O avião com a cantora Mariana Fagundes, do hit 'Peão Todo Tatuado' , precisou fazer um pouso de emergência em Goiânia após o gerador parar, segundo a cantora. Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, ela contou que seguia rumo ao Rio de Janeiro quando o avião apresentou problemas (assista acima) . Apesar do susto, ela conseguiu seguir viagem após a troca da aeronave e tranquilizou os fãs.

O pouso aconteceu na manhã desta quinta-feira (4), quando a cantora embarcou em um voo no Pará, onde se apresentou na 11ª ExpoCanaã.

"Fizemos um showzão, acabamos o show e entramos no avião rumo ao Rio de Janeiro. Tivemos um probleminha sério no avião, parou o gerador e fizemos um pouso de emergência aqui em Goiânia, mas tudo certo, graças a Deus", disse ela.

Depois de trocar de avião, a cantora seguiu rumo ao Rio de Janeiro, onde gravou o programa Domingão com o Huck na companhia do cantor Jeninho , seu parceiro no hit eletrofunk que tocou por todo o Brasil.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Agência Nacional de Aviação (Anac) para saber se o incidente é investigado e aguarda retorno.

Avião com Mariana Fagundes faz pouso de emergência em Goiânia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

De acordo com o piloto Benjamin Neto, a falha no gerador não significa que o avião "perdeu o motor", mas que o piloto provavelmente declarou prioridade para o pouso. Segundo ele, existe um livro de referência nas cabines das aeronaves, o Quick Reference Handbook (QRH), que determina o que deve ser feito quando determinado equipamento apresenta falha.

"Provavelmente, nesse checklist da aeronave estava determinado o pouso imediato quando esse gerador falha. [...] Então, o gerador falhar, pode desenvolver uma falha elétrica que poderia desencadear vários outros problemas" , disse ele.

Ainda segundo ele, a falha no gerador não é um evento comum e, na verdade, é raro, pois antes de decolar é preciso fazer uma checagem para verificar se todos os equipamentos estão funcionando corretamente na aeronave.

articles.title: Philippines court orders arrest of VP Sara Duterte over 'assassin' remarks targeting President's family
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A Philippine court on Friday issued an arrest warrant for Vice President Sara Duterte over three counts of grave threats involving President Ferdinand.
articles.body: A Philippine court on Friday issued an arrest warrant for Vice President Sara Duterte over three counts of grave threats involving President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., the first lady and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, deepening a political feud between the country’s two most powerful families.The Quezon City Regional Trial Court issued the warrant and set bail at 120,000 pesos (approximately Rs 1 lakh 80 thousand) for each of the three charges, according to the court order.Duterte’s lawyer, Paul Lawrence Lim, said she had no intention of evading the law and would continue to pursue all available legal remedies.The case relates to remarks Duterte made in November 2024, when she said she had spoken to an assassin and instructed him to kill Marcos, his wife and Romualdez if she herself were killed. Duterte has denied threatening them.The criminal case comes as Duterte faces a separate impeachment trial before the Philippine Senate. The alleged threats are among the accusations contained in the impeachment proceedings, which also include allegations of misuse of public funds. Duterte has denied wrongdoing.Duterte’s legal team had previously challenged the criminal proceedings on jurisdictional grounds, arguing that she was a sitting impeachable official. Legal experts, however, said the criminal case and impeachment proceedings could proceed simultaneously because they involve different legal standards.The Justice Department filed the three grave-threat charges against Duterte in August after an investigation by the National Bureau of Investigation. A separate inciting-to-sedition complaint was dismissed.The arrest warrant adds another major legal challenge for Duterte, who is the daughter of former President Rodrigo Duterte and has been viewed as a potential contender in the 2028 presidential election. articles.title: Russia starved, tortured a US Marine for 4 years — stop treating Putin like an ally
articles.summary: Some of conservative media’s loudest voices insist Russia is a friend. But look at what the Russians did to one of our countrymen.
articles.body:
Russia finally released ailing former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman after 1,666 days in captivity. The man who came home was a shadow of his former self: emaciated, frail, and denied proper medical care for the entirety of his imprisonment.

By the time Russia let him go, Gilman had fallen into a catatonic state, suffered from severe pneumonia, and had to be fed through a tube. His family warned that he was on the verge of death.

That is the condition an American citizen was in when Vladimir Putin’s regime handed him back on what it called a “humanitarian basis.”

Gilman was so starved during his years in Russian custody that, according to President Trump, the one thing he asked for when he got on the plane home was a cheeseburger. It is shocking to think that one of the “few and the proud,” held for more than four years by a country some of conservative media’s loudest voices insist is a friend, came out of custody asking for a basic meal.

Sadly, Gilman’s is not an isolated case. At least 10 Americans have been confirmed by our own government to be held under harsh conditions against their will in Russia. Five of them — Aleksandr Antonov, David Barnes, Olga Jezler, Andre Khachatoorian and Chuck Zimmerman — have been identified by advocates as meeting the U.S. government’s own criteria for wrongful detention. Every one of them is reported to be facing serious medical concerns like the ones that nearly killed Gilman.

What kind of country jails American citizens, starves them, withholds basic health care and then expects us to smile and pretend everything is fine when one is returned?

That is precisely what a loud faction on the right keeps asking us to do.

Prominent voices, including Candace Owens and Tucker Carlson among them, have spent years telling their audiences that Russia is a traditional, high-functioning Christian society with admirable values and world-class health care. In May, Owens traveled to sanctioned Russia to speak at a state-sponsored conference. She came home praising the wonders of the Russian health care system .

Russian healthcare is so great that they just sent an American Marine home catatonic, starving, and riddled with pneumonia after denying him medical care for years.

I heard what Russian captivity does to people firsthand when I interviewed Ukrainian prisoners of war who had survived Russian custody. They described systematic beatings, starvation and daily torture. The first thing they had to do in custody was come to understand that a human being could be treated this way by another person. It is heartbreaking, but over 95 percent of Ukrainian prisoners of war and 85 percent of captured civilians are tortured or mistreated by Russia, according to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

That is why a group of Ukrainian prisoners of war recently pleaded their case before an informal gathering of the United Nations Security Council. Russia’s deputy U.N. Ambassador Maria Zabolotskaya responded to their testimony by calling it “a disinformation campaign against Russia.”

I have heard the stories directly from former Ukrainian prisoners of war. Ukraine’s military intelligence agency showed me pictures of a Ukrainian prisoner who had been cut open, without anesthesia, for a surgical procedure, leaving behind a massive scar across his belly and a “Z” — the symbol of Russian invaders — that looked like it was burned into his skin. He was practically branded like cattle.

A Ukrainian plastic surgeon has since removed the “Z” free of charge so the man didn’t have to live with a constant reminder of the torture he endured while in Russian captivity.

Will American media voices keep entertaining the fiction that Vladimir Putin is a man we can trust, while American citizens are still being held hostage in Russia? The plane that brought Gilman home should have been filled with every remaining American in Russian custody. Putin does not become a good man, let alone someone the U.S. government should thank, simply because he released one American his own military had tortured.

I’m not calling for war or abandoning diplomacy. I am asking Americans to wake up. Putin’s Russia is not America’s ally. It is an adversary that brutalizes our citizens and counts on our commentators to explain it away, along with Russia’s own state sponsored media organs that push propaganda all day long.

The right thing — the America First thing — is to bring every American home who is still in Russian captivity, and to understand that Russia is deliberately depriving Americans of their liberty and torturing them, just as it has done to thousands of Ukrainians throughout the course of this war.

Laura Loomer is an investigative journalist and the founder of Loomered.com. She recently reported from Ukraine, where she interviewed Ukrainian prisoners of war released from Russian captivity, and President Volodymyr Zelensky.

articles.title: One of history's most famous battles could be rewritten by long-lost papal letter
articles.summary: A lost papal letter recently found in Vatican archives suggests Pope Alexander II backed William the Conqueror's invasion over England's ties to a rival pope.
articles.body: A lost letter from a pope could rewrite the story of one of history's most famous battles — nearly 1,000 years after it was fought. The University of East Anglia announced the new research, which sheds light on the Norman Conquest of England in 1066, in August. Professor Tom Licence was examining historical records when he came across previously overlooked excerpts from a lost papal letter that was preserved in the Vatican archives, he said. ROYAL DECREE FROM NOTORIOUS 'SPIDER KING' REDISCOVERED IN VERY UNEXPECTED LOCATION The letter suggests Pope Alexander II may have backed William the Conqueror's invasion of England because the English had sided with his rival — offering a new explanation for the events that led to the Battle of Hastings. In the letter, Alexander described England as being led astray by an "evil head" and used striking religious language that Licence said branded the English as "followers of Satan." The Battle of Hastings, one of the most consequential battles in English history, has traditionally been viewed as a fight over who had the rightful claim to the English throne: King Harold II or William of Normandy. It has not typically been viewed as part of a broader political and religious struggle involving the papacy, but Licence said the events of 1066 may have been closely tied to a bitter power struggle between Pope Alexander II and his rival, the antipope Honorius II. ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MASSIVE ARTIFACT DEPICTING PHARAOH THOUGHT TO HAVE CHALLENGED MOSES IN EXODUS Licence's research suggests England may have sided with Honorius, potentially giving Alexander another reason to support the Norman invasion. Licence told Fox News Digital he wasn't personally surprised by the connection he made. "Which papal faction England was aligning with at any given time is always in the back of my mind," the professor said. "I suspect, however, that most historians working on the Norman Conquest are not looking at Rome that closely," he added. ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MYSTERIOUS FACE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES IN BOOK OF REVELATION CITY Honorius II may not be a familiar name to many — but Licence said he remained a "serious contender" in the papal power struggle, even after his position weakened in 1064. "In fact, it looked like [Honorius II] was going to make a comeback in 1065," he said. "Sometimes it just takes someone to come along and join the dots." "Read in that context, the letter from Pope Alexander about England being led astray under an 'evil head' made sense at last. It was never clear to historians in the past what Alexander was referring to." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Licence said he was "confident" that the English moved away from backing Alexander II, which would have amounted to "a withdrawal of support." "It's less clear to me that England openly declared support for Honorius," he said. "Alexander's rhetoric about the English being led from the path of truth by an 'evil head' — and calling them 'followers of Satan' — suggests, at the very least, that they were leaning that way." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS He said that specializing in both fields allowed him to make the connection. "Sometimes it just takes someone to come along and join the dots," he said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Most scholars working on the Norman Conquest aren't specialists in ecclesiastical history, and they may not, in any case, be looking closely at papal politics." Licence said his findings change the understanding of Alexander's role in the events of 1066. "This discovery therefore changes how we think about Alexander's motives in 1066," he said. "He wanted regime change in England." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The findings are detailed in Licence's new book, "Harold: Warrior King."

articles.title: FCC asks court to reject Disney lawsuit over ABC TV station licenses
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission asked a federal judge to toss out Disney’s lawsuit seeking to block the agency’s early review ​of licenses for the entertainment giant’s eight company-owned ABC stations.
articles.body: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission asked a federal judge on Thursday to toss out Disney’s lawsuit seeking to block the agency’s early review ​of licenses for the entertainment giant’s eight company-owned ABC stations. The FCC said if Disney were successful, it would prevent the commission from analyzing evidence in its ongoing investigation and hobble the agency’s “efforts to investigate and resolve serious allegations that Disney has engaged in unlawful discrimination.” The case is a test of free speech rights for broadcasters. President Donald Trump has called repeatedly for ABC to lose its licenses over programming he dislikes. FCC Chair Brendan Carr ordered the early reviews in April, even though the ‌stations’ license renewals ⁠were not scheduled to be considered before October 2028. The FCC had not ordered an early review in more than 50 years before April. Carr has said he has not made a decision on whether to refer Disney’s licenses for a hearing. The reviews were ordered a day after Trump urged ABC to ​fire late-night host Jimmy ⁠Kimmel. U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan in Washington has set an October 6 hearing on the lawsuit. The FCC has agreed to provide at least 48 hours’ notice before ​issuing an order to refer Disney’s ABC licenses for a public hearing. Trump has repeatedly urged broadcasters to drop comedy or news programs he dislikes or which have joked about or criticized him or his administration. He has also called on the FCC to strip stations of licenses after criticizing news and other programming. The FCC also said the case should be before a federal appeals court in Washington rather than the district court. On Sunday, Trump called for the FCC to rebuke or punish Comcast-owned NBC’s journalist Kristen Welker after she noted that the Republican president’s success in endorsing political candidates has been mixed. Carr has been investigating diversity practices at Comcast since February 2025 and not ruled out subjecting its NBC licenses to an early review. Broadcast stations need FCC licenses to use public airwaves. While license revocations are extremely rare, critics say the threat of losing a license can pressure broadcasters and raise concerns about government interference in editorial and programming decisions. Networks have broad First Amendment protections over programming choices. Disney, which declined to comment Thursday, said in its suit the FCC was seeking to coerce and retaliate against “a network that refuses to bow to the ⁠administration’s ​demands,” calling the agency’s actions an “extraordinary assault on free speech.”

articles.title: How Oasis fans cracked the Celtic Park gigs code in chip shop video
articles.summary: Internet sleuths spotted sets of numbers in posters suggesting the map co-ordinates for Celtic's Parkhead stadium in Glasgow.
articles.body:
Oasis fans have uncovered a set of cryptic clues in a promo video from the band, suggesting that they will stage gigs at Celtic Park in Glasgow next year.

The Manchester rockers released the 23-second teaser on their social media accounts, showing two boys in what appears to be a Scottish chip shop.

Internet sleuths spotted sets of numbers in posters around the chippy which they worked out to be the map co-ordinates for Celtic's Parkhead stadium.

It has fuelled speculation that the band will be playing at the venue next year- possibly as the first date of a new tour.

It follows the Gallagher brothers' hugely successful reunion tour which saw them perform at 41 sold-out stadium shows in 14 countries.

This included three dates at Murrayfield Stadium, Edinburgh, in August 2025, when they played to 200,000 fans.

The clues hinting at a Celtic Park gig include an advert for a £55.84 family chippy bundle and a poster for radio station Sol FM 98 92.

The numbers spell out the 55.849892N latitude of the stadium.

There is also a sticker on the fridge saying it should be kept at -4, a poster saying the daily special is priced at £2.05 and a taxi number featuring the area code 638.

These numbers together are -4.205638W - Celtic Park's longitude.

More clues: Robert Carlyle, Irn Bru and deep-fried Mars Bar

Other Scottish clues include the actor Robert Carlyle, who features in the video for Oasis song Little by Little which plays on a TV in the background.

The chip shop fridge is filled with Irn Bru and other AG Barr brands.

One of the boys also hands over a Mars Bar to be deep fried - a Scottish chippy delicacy.

Fans have also posted theories about other "clues" on social media.

One said the position of the two boys is similar to the positions of Noel and Liam Gallagher on the front of the Definitely Maybe album, with the fridge being in a similar position to the window.

An announcement has been rumoured to coincide with the release of Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger, a documentary covering the band's reunion tour.

Recent rumours have suggested that any Celtic Park concerts could take place immediately after the Scottish football season ends in late May with Knebworth also believed to be on the cards .

The Gallagher brothers' affection for Celtic is well documented, stemming from their family's Irish roots.

The Oasis classic Roll With It has become an unofficial Celtic anthem, having first been adopted by supporters around the 1997 League Cup final.

And Noel famously attended the Old Firm game in 2000 when Celtic beat Rangers 6-2.

Celtic Park has not hosted any concerts for a number of years with the last being Wet, Wet Wet in 1997.

Other noteable gigs there have been Rod Stewart, Status Quo and Joe Cocker in 1991, Bryan Adams and Prince in 1992, U2 and Utah Saints in 1993.

Rod Stewart performed there again in 2014 during the Opening Ceremony for the Commonwealth Games.

Glasgow's Hampden Park has become the city's main concert stadium over the past three decades.

articles.title: South Korea mulls ‘contributions’ in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Seoul heavily affected by closure of strategic waterway and under heavy US pressure for participation against Iran.
articles.body:
South Korea is mulling “contributions” to the freedom of navigation ⁠in the Strait of Hormuz, the presidential office said.

The office said in a statement released on Friday that various options regarding providing assistance in securing the strategic waterway were being considered.

The United States has been pressuring Seoul and other allies over their refusal to join its war against Iran, which has seen Tehran limiting maritime traffic in the strait – a key route for global oil supplies.

Local broadcaster JTBC reported on Thursday that South Korea’s government was “leaning toward” dispatching troops to the strait and reviewing details ahead of seeking parliamentary approval.

The presidential office was eager to state that no decision has yet been made, although that effort appeared to spread further confusion.

An unnamed official told reporters that “nothing has been decided” and that Seoul would consider domestic legal procedures, military readiness and parliamentary approval.

“South Korea may be able to make military contributions to global efforts to ensure free navigation through the strait, as long as such contributions do not compromise its military readiness,” the official said.

The president’s office then issued a statement saying: “References made during today’s briefing regarding military contributions – such as combat participation, non-combat roles, and search operations – were merely general descriptions of various options.

“Please be advised that nothing has been decided yet concerning actual contributions,” it added.

Any military deployment by South Korea requires a decision by the National Security Council, a resolution at a cabinet meeting, and consent from the National Assembly.

The ongoing discussion “has not reached the stage of seeking parliamentary approval and no final decision has been made,” the official from the presidential office said.

President Lee Jae Myung may discuss options regarding the Strait of Hormuz when he meets French President Emmanuel Macron next week, he added.

Public support for involvement in the Middle East may be limited. A Gallup ‌Korea poll from March found 55 percent of people were opposed to sending South Korean warships to the strait.

However, South Korea has been heavily affected by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The country relied on the supplies transiting the waterway for 61 percent of its crude oil imports and 54 percent of its naphtha imports last year.

It is also under pressure from the US, its most important ally.

President Donald Trump said in August that he had cancelled US-South Korea joint military exercises in part because South Korea had declined to help the US in its war against Iran.

Afterwards, the South Korean government said it would pursue a deployment to the strait only after the US-Iran war ends.

The official from the presidential office insisted claims that South Korea has provided no assistance related to the Strait of Hormuz were “not true”, saying Seoul had long discussed practical contributions with the international community.

In late 2019, South Korea’s military expanded the deployment of its anti-piracy unit from Somalia to the area around Hormuz after the US pressed for help to guard oil tankers.

articles.title: 25 years later, Britney Spears’ 2001 VMAs performance still mesmerizes
articles.summary: 25 years ago the starlet made pop culture history with a 7-foot long, 20-pound albino Burmese python named “Banana.” Here’s how it happened.
articles.body: Britney Spears was ready to drop a new single. But how? It was 2001, and Spears was the biggest pop star in the world, with her 10-time-platinum sophomore album, “Oops! I Did It Again” behind her. The public would be expecting something suitably huge. They got something even bigger than that. Spears decided to deliver the new song, “I’m a Slave 4 U,” live on stage at New York City’s Metropolitan Opera house, during the annual MTV Video Music Awards. There would be no concert previews or early radio release or teaser clips to prepare the way. The world had to sit down, tune in, and see what might unfold. What came next set a standard that was genuinely, historically impossible to follow — a risk-taking spectacle that could only have happened at the turn of this century, in those last years before mass media fragmented into millions of personal screens fed by millions of personal cameras, before constant performing and constant exposure took their painful, visible toll on Spears herself. A 19-year-old Spears stepped casually out of a gilded metal cage, where a white tiger sat behind her. She wore a moss green bra-like top, aquamarine disco shorts, and bedazzled nude-hued boots. Around her was a sea of dancers in animalistic garb — zebra-striped body paint, dual-toned neon wigs — as a pulsating beat produced by The Neptunes blared through the venue and television screens nationwide. And there was the snake — a 7-foot long, 20-pound albino Burmese python named “Banana” that the star seductively draped across her shoulders for the last portion of the performance. That image of Spears in jaw-dropping form, wielding a magnetic stare, and commanding not just the stage but the entire world watching at home defined the singer’s peak as a performer. It also stands in stark contrast with the life Spears now lives today. Since being released from a years-long conservatorship where her personal and professional life was controlled by her now estranged father Jamie Spears, the singer has expressed countless times — via social media and her published memoir — that she has no desire to perform ever again. “The reason this performance has such a legacy is because there’s never been an artist as famous as Britney since Britney,” said Amber Horsburgh, a writer and culture critic. “The technology at the time, the appointment viewing aspect, the importance of MTV, and the Britney Spears MTV collision of it all — it had such a chokehold on the culture at the time.” Stepping into her own The jungle-goddess costume was the work of designers Kurt Swanson and Bart Mueller. “Because we had already done so much together, there was a huge level of trust and how specific looks came together was kind of kinetic,” Mueller wrote in an email. “The lyrics inspired the choreography, which fueled the concepts, and then there was Britney’s performance and energy. It all shaped our design directions. Everything was custom right down to the nude mesh, lucite wedge heel boots that we had hand-sewn crystal anklets to, including a shining sequined serpent wrapping around one leg to punch up the Eve reference.” Showing skin was a key part of the overall look, but there were also a number of blink-and-you’d-miss it details that brought the ensemble together together. Every piece — the pleated wrap top, the shorts adorned with trailing shards of silk chiffon — was hand-dyed or painted and then covered in Swarovski crystals. “We were crystal- obsessed back then,” said Swanson. “We even had Swarovski tattoo body jewelry applied to her skin.” What the designers hadn’t considered in putting the outfit together was that a live tiger would be joining the singer on stage. The rehearsals in the leadup to the show had been human-only, Swanson said. “The day of the VMAs at the tech rehearsal was the first time any of us had been with the wild animals,” he recalled. The tiger’s trainer — Bhagavan “Doc” Antle, long before his appearance in “Tiger King” made him famous — instructed them on the protocol for sharing the stage with a huge, inherently wild animal. “It kind of boiled down to staying out of the animal’s sight lines and that there couldn’t be anything to distract it,” Swanson said. “Nothing that dangled or moved in a way that might attract the tiger’s attention.” “Well,” Mueller said, “Britney’s entire look, with the dancing trailing fabric and feathers, her hair….Britney was basically a shiny life-sized cat toy for one giant cat!” Spears’s head choreographer, the 18-year-old Wade Robson, slightly reworked the staging with Antle to keep Spears out of the sightline. Swanson and Mueller were eager to be a part of shaping a new sartorial era for the singer. They also designed her look in the “I’m a Slave 4 U” music video that premiered weeks later, incorporating similar motifs — like bold jewel hues and flowing chiffon detailing — so the two projects could feel connected. “We loved the colors of the jungle, iridescent beetle green, electric colors of exotic birds, insects, flowers,” Swanson said. “Fuschia, emerald, turquoise, acid yellow all became the palette for this performance. We loved the iconic curvy silhouettes of jungle warrior princesses in the art of Frank Frazetta and Boris Vallejo. We were obsessed with traditional belly dancing and the way fabric moved and jewelry and ornamentation would jingle and accentuate the shape of the choreography.” “The way that Britney moves was always what pushed our design,” Mueller said. “The way she performed ‘Slave’ specifically, shaped the look.” Tech in a totally different world Spears’ MTV performance was also one of the first set-designing jobs led by Ray Winkler, the CEO and design director of STUFISH Entertainment Architects. Winkler recalled having only three weeks to work with MTV and Spears’s creative team to produce the stage design, at a time when digital collaboration was in its early infancy. There were no pre-production Zoom meetings, but rather the juggle of scheduling international calls and waiting for another part of the world to wake up in order to receive vital feedback. “Those days meant hard core sketching, sketching again, scanning, and believe it or not, we had to fax things,” Winkler said. “LA, New York, London. How do you align? You didn’t have the internet to tell you what time it was exactly where, you know, or people couldn’t just respond, say, “Oh, I can’t do this..” What Winkler landed on with Robson, was the concept of elevated welded cages that the singer and her crew of dancers would dance around on. “I was very worried about the welds of the cage being strong enough to contain the tiger,” said Winkler. Ahead of the televised performance, he said, the animal handlers fed the feline “a lot of raw steaks” to ensure it wouldn’t be hungry on stage. “I don’t know if you would get away with that in this day and age.” “I call that time sort of within an envelope of innocence because social media didn’t exist,” Winkler said. “We — the team, producers, artists, production — had pretty much exclusive access to how this would be portrayed to the wider audiences because nobody in the live audience had a mobile phone that they could record it. The director’s cut was the only cut that was made available.” That level of control helped give the performance its enduring power. “It was very, very tailor-made to her,” Winkler said. “ It was made for what I would still call the analog MTV consumer. And I often wonder whether this had been done in this day and age now if it would have the same impact, just because it has to vie with so many other flashpoints of interest, and the attention span, which was already terrible in the early noughties, is completely evaporated now. She was an icon at the time, and still is, to be clear. But at the time that this happened, it cemented her status as somebody who was willing to take risks, and it was a big risk. But she pulled it off.” Debunking the pop puppet myth Brian Friedman, one of Spears’ longtime choreographers and dancers, knew even before they hit the stage at the VMAs that year that “I’m a Slave 4 U” would strike a chord with listeners. The sultry dance moves seen on stage and in the music video was also one of the first major credited choreographing gigs Friedman had received at that point in his career. Alongside Robson, the pair went on to create some of Spears’ most recognizable dance breaks, still recreated and performed by fans to this day. “I was completely obsessed with the song the second that I heard it and the choreographic process with Wade and I — it just flowed,” Friedman said. “When we first played around with the choreography at her house, it was just undeniable that it was going to be a smash. Never did I think that it was going to be what ‘Thriller’ and ‘Rhythm Nation’ were to me as a kid growing up. It truly has stood the test of time and become one of those landmark pop dance moments.” Friedman was clued into every creative update as it came, including the inclusion of the live snake and tiger. “We’re both maximalists when it comes to visuals,” he said. “She had done so many performances that it gets to the point where you’re thinking, well, what haven’t we done? What can we do to stand out and make a memorable performance?” Friedman is also acutely aware that now there’s a new lens to look through when people revisit a Britney Spears performance. In her 2023 memoir “The Woman In Me,” Spears described the conservatorship and her then grueling performance schedule as the “death to my creativity as an artist.” Friedman remembers a period of time however — pre-conservatorship — when Spears was in control of her career, and witnessed her thrive. “A lot of people feel that she was some sort of manufactured pop star or a puppet in some sort of way, and that couldn’t have been further from the truth. Especially in that era, she was such a hard worker,” he shared. “Her schedule was being pushed on her, but the work ethic wasn’t. She truly loved what she was doing. She loved being on stage, and she loved to sweat and be in the dance studio in rehearsals with the dancers.” A void in the pop-sphere Could there be another Britney Spears? Should there be one? Latter-day stars politely shrug off the comparisons; fans are chastened by having witnessed how fame — and a craving for control — undid their favorite performer. “She has made it very clear that she doesn’t want to be performing right now, so I honor that in her and respect her wishes,” Friedman said. Still, he said, the sight of Spears’s idol Madonna flourishing at the age of 68 leaves him hoping Britney might someday get back onstage again. Horsburgh, the writer and culture critic, said that Spears’s past triumphs stand on their own. “Of course you miss Britney Spears, and of course you want another album, and you want another tour — but I actually hope that she never goes back to the stage ever again if she doesn’t want to, and her fanbase and the general public can understand and respect that,” said Horbough. “Clearly, she doesn’t communicate often, but when she does, she’s been very clear — ‘I’m not performing ever again. I’m finished.’ We as fans have to ask less right now, not ask more of her. She’s got such a huge legacy and such a catalog of incredible music, incredible visuals, incredible albums — that legacy should be preserved.”

articles.title: Germany’s far right AfD eyes election breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt
articles.summary: The nationalist party is poised to win more than 40 percent of the votes in the state.
articles.body:
Mario Jung does not fit the profile of a political hardliner. The 59-year-old banking clerk, who lives in Magdeburg in eastern Germany, has voted for the country’s conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in the past.

But he blames former Chancellor Angela Merkel for pushing the CDU to the left and on Sunday, in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, he will back the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party.

“I am a conservative, and the main reason for me to vote for the (far-right) AfD is the economy,” he told Al Jazeera.

He also agrees with the AfD’s hardline immigration policy.

“All illegal immigrants, those whose applications have been denied, and criminal immigrants as well – they have to be deported; there is no question about it,” he said.

The regional elections pose a test for Germany’s political establishment, with the AfD in contention for top positions in the state government.

In Saxony-Anhalt, it is poised to become the first far-right force to head a German state government since World War II, with the AfD’s leading candidate, Ulrich Siegmund.

He was dubbed “Germany’s most dangerous man” by the influential magazine Der Spiegel. Before becoming a politician for the AfD, Siegmund was a member of the CDU.

The party has been classified as “far-right extremist” in Saxony-Anhalt by Germany’s domestic intelligence service. The AfD is leading the state by a wide margin in the polls, expected to win more than 40 percent of the votes.

The conservative CDU is far behind at just above 20 percent, followed by the Left Party at 12 percent, the Social Democrats at 7 percent and the Greens at 5 percent. Depending on which smaller parties clear the threshold to enter parliament, the other parties could potentially form a majority without the AfD. But German Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) recently ruled out cooperation with both the Left Party and the AfD, a party whose officials have used Nazi slogans.

In its election platform, titled “The Country First”, the AfD calls for the abolition of the right to asylum, the confiscation of cash and assets of asylum seekers and mass deportations.

Anyone who insults German identity or the “historical-cultural entity Germany” could face a prison sentence, according to the campaign. The party also seeks to ban the “Antifa” movement, cancel public broadcasting and reverse the shift towards renewable energy.

Founded in 2013 as a Eurosceptic party in the aftermath of the European Union financial crisis, it gained ground during Merkel’s 2015 decision to admit about a million refugees, many of them Syrian.

It has since shifted further right, dominated today by a nationalist wing and hardline factions in the east, hardline immigration positions and opposition to sanctions on Russia.

The AfD has also repeatedly politicised attacks by asylum seekers or Germans with foreign descent.

While critics argue that such incidents receive excessive media focus, the deadly car attack at Berlin’s Pride parade in July keeps pushing the topic into the headlines. AfD blamed the “catastrophic migration policy of the last few years”, but the attacker had been born in Germany.

Experts have put forward various hypotheses to explain the party’s popularity .

Last year, it became the second-largest party in the Bundestag, securing 21 percent of the vote in federal elections.

In Germany’s eastern states, which were formerly part of the German Democratic Republic (GDR) and the Eastern Bloc and underwent a radical transition after reunification, structural factors are at play, analysts say.

The region is characterised by a lack of jobs, a shortage of local doctors, the decline of public transportation, depopulated villages, and a persistent perception that the eastern states are governed by distant liberal elites in Berlin.

Thomas Biebricher, a professor at Goethe University Frankfurt, believes the main reason for the AfD’s success “is widespread dissatisfaction with the political situation, the federal government and the overall economic situation in the country. At the same time, the AfD has managed to nominate a lead candidate who is doing a very good job,” he told Al Jazeera.

While the party is often seen as most popular among workers, its success is also linked to “parts of the capitalist class” who are pushing a neoliberal agenda, Biebricher said.

“There are influential AfD supporters who believe that capitalism is over-regulated, that taxes should be lowered, and that the state, overall, should simply intervene less.

“If it were to enter government, it would be the first time since 1945 that a party with a far-right agenda would enter government at the state level,” he added. It would “also cause considerable damage to Germany’s image”.

For several years, the CDU has been debating nationwide how to deal with the AfD. At the local level, the “principle of non-cooperation” – also known as the “firewall”- has already been abandoned.

Martin Schroder, a professor of social sciences at Saarland University, believes that the AfD’s migration policy is crucial for its success.

Together with a team, he conducted a study based on data from 2014 to 2024.

“Concerns about immigration explain support for the AfD nearly 10 times as much as actual or perceived economic disadvantage,” he told Al Jazeera.

Another key election takes place on September 20 in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where the AfD is also polling at about 37 percent.

Like Saxony-Anhalt, the northeastern state was formerly part of the GDR. Berlin will also go to the polls that day. In the capital, which is also one of Germany’s 16 federal states, the CDU currently leads with 21 percent, followed by the Left Party at 19 percent and the AfD at 18 percent.

articles.title: Sheep stolen from Jeremy Clarkson's Diddly Squat Farm
articles.summary: Thames Valley Police said 11 sheep were stolen from the farm in Chadlington.
articles.body:
Eleven sheep have been stolen from Diddly Squat Farm belonging to presenter Jeremy Clarkson.

Thames Valley Police said it received reports on Wednesday that the animals had been taken from the farm in Chadlington, Oxfordshire, within the last 10 days.

It said officers spoke with Clarkson at the scene on Thursday, adding that no arrests had been made and anyone with information should get in contact.

The 66-year-old told The Sun he discovered the animals were missing when he went to count his flock with Clarkson's Farm co-star Kaleb Cooper.

The former Top Gear and The Grand Tour presenter appealed for those responsible to "put them back".

He told The Sun that he believed the sheep were worth more than £2,000 at market, and added that he was worried some in other fields of his farm may have also been stolen.

Diddly Squat Farm has gained attention as the focal point for Amazon Prime Video series Clarkson's Farm and he told the newspaper the theft had been done at night or during a day when the farm was not being filmed for the show, when he said there was "a film crew here all the time" and "a drone in the air".

Listen to the latest news from Oxfordshire

Asked whether he believed the show had made his farm a target, Clarkson said: "It's more likely to make you a target than less, but I still don't think they've been stolen because they're on Diddly Squat.

"How can you (stop it) if someone's determined to steal your livestock?

"This is 1,000 acres, it's a big farm. Anyone could be anywhere and you wouldn't know."

articles.title: Guernsey-Jersey ferry's season ends early due to engine problem
articles.summary: Inter-island ferry crossings are cancelled for the rest of the season due to the engine issue.
articles.body:
A ferry company has taken the "difficult decision" to end its season early to avoid passenger uncertainty after problems with its only ship's starboard main engine.

Islands Unlimited said it would take too long to source, install and test a replacement engine part for the 316 seat high-speed passenger catamaran San Pawl.

The daily service between Guernsey and Jersey, with weekend sailings to Alderney, was due to run until Sunday 18 October, but was halted last week .

Islands Unlimited said the cause of the problem was found after extensive technical investigation and it recognised "the disruption and disappointment this will cause, particularly for passengers with upcoming travel plans".

Suspended ferry causes problems for sports clubs

Ferry problems may affect Pride attendance

Ferry service remains suspended after engine fault

Ferry sailings suspended after engine failure

Operations manager Jack Kitching said: "This was an unexpected and unforeseeable technical failure, and our team has explored every realistic option to get San Pawl back into service.

"Unfortunately, the timescales involved in sourcing and installing a replacement engine now extend beyond the end of our planned season."

The service was launched in 2025 and recorded more than 30,000 passenger movements in 2026.

Kitching said the company fully intended to return in 2027 and would complete the necessary engine replacement and associated works over the coming months and "build greater resilience into our operation".
